definition: auto-sklearn is AutoML for scikit-learn: it searches models, preprocessing and hyperparameters for you and builds an ensemble.
details: Developed by the AutoML groups at the University of Freiburg and Leibniz University Hannover (Matthias Feurer, Frank Hutter et al.).

explainer.lead: How to install auto-sklearn, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: AutoML.org — University of Freiburg and Leibniz University Hannover.

quickstart.python:
import autosklearn.classification
from sklearn.datasets import load_digits

X, y = load_digits(return_X_y=True)
automl = autosklearn.classification.AutoSklearnClassifier(time_left_for_this_task=300)
automl.fit(X, y)
print(automl.leaderboard())

explainer.inAi: Get a strong tabular baseline in minutes to compare against hand-built or LLM-based approaches.
explainer.jsNote: auto-sklearn is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: It is like a robot assistant that tries many recipes and picks the best combination for you.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers hand it a dataset and a time budget and get back a tuned ensemble rather than tuning scikit-learn estimators manually. A pitfall is trusting the automatic result without checking whether the search budget was enough.
tiers.paperLevel: An AutoML system from the AutoML groups at the University of Freiburg and Leibniz University Hannover that searches models, preprocessing and hyperparameters and builds an ensemble. Quality depends on the search budget and the scikit-learn estimator space.

explainer.example: Given a tabular dataset and a time limit, auto-sklearn returns an ensemble of tuned scikit-learn pipelines ready for prediction.
